title: Aerospace Folktales
subtitle: Family, engineering, unemployment, and the ordered interior
introduction: A rights-aware research preview following five source-described movements within Allan Sekula’s 1973 photo-text work. The work photographs remain metadata-only until reuse permission is documented. The shelf below publishes no inferred influence: only the Clark record for the work itself is shown while candidate relations await named librarian review.

clusters.title: The company’s story
clusters.narrative: Steve Edwards describes an opening group built from a Lockheed chairman’s words and corporate newsletter imagery. This reader names that movement without reproducing the photographs or treating the corporate material as a library-book association.

clusters.title: Outside the plant
clusters.narrative: The published analysis follows Sekula’s father and a friend at the empty Lockheed plant, then moves by detail, portrait, and apartment façade toward the domestic interior. The rights-pending frame preserves that sequence as metadata rather than substituting unrelated imagery.

clusters.title: Work returns home
clusters.narrative: Sekula’s oral history connects the project to his father’s unemployment and his return to the family milieu. Edwards’s analysis attends to domestic labor and to engineering order displaced into the home. These are source-grounded descriptions of the work, not claims about nearby books.

clusters.title: Everything in its place
clusters.narrative: The analysis describes carefully ordered rooms, models of aircraft, and three page spreads from a nuclear-effects manual. A promising Clark shelf record exists, but it remains excluded here until a librarian reviews whether the photographed physical copy can be identified.

clusters.title: Four voices, one unsettled account
clusters.period_label: Image, sound, and commentary · editorial label
clusters.narrative: Generali describes the original version as a disassembled movie of 142 prints and titles, four conversations, and written commentary; Getty identifies surviving print, audio, and research components. The interface links outward while permission for reproductions is pending.
